reading.body:
CyrusOne Lebanon occupies 400,000 square feet with 12 megawatts of published IT capacity. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common baseline for mixed enterprise and cloud workloads, 12 megawatts would supply approximately 300 racks. The site holds security and compliance certifications spanning data protection standards, healthcare and financial regulation, federal information systems governance, and environmental management.

This facility ranks first among the 8 Ohio data centers with published power figures on this site, representing 20 percent of the state's total announced capacity of 60.4 megawatts. Ohio's mapped data center footprint includes 77 facilities, of which only eight have disclosed their power consumption publicly. The campus sits in a state where capacity transparency remains limited outside published operator disclosures.

The published capacity does not indicate whether this campus is configured for AI training, inference, or general-purpose cloud and enterprise hosting. The certifications qualify the facility for regulated workloads including government systems and sensitive personal data, but do not specify accelerator density, GPU inventory, memory bandwidth, or cooling architecture. Whether this campus represents available AI-ready capacity or serves other workload classes cannot be determined from published specifications.
